_note: Card copy for the guided tour. Three layers per scene: what you are looking at, what just happened, why it matters. Counts are placeholders — no figure is written here by hand. Two rules are enforced by tests: no term appears before the scene that introduces it, and the first sentence of any card avoids the trade words.

scenes.title: You hand the system its rules
scenes.l1: This is the request: market data, plus the rules — "laws" — the caller declares for how answers may be computed.
scenes.l2: This caller forgot {missing} of the {total} laws.
scenes.l3: Nothing outside this box will ever influence the result. Watch what the system does about it — it will not guess.

scenes.title: The receipt: every answer, or a named refusal
scenes.l1: Read it like a store receipt: every line is either a computed number or a refusal with the exact reason printed.
scenes.l2: {computed} computed, {refused} refused — and the receipt names the missing law for each.
scenes.l3: No AI was involved yet. This is deterministic code: same input, same receipt, same hash — forever.

scenes.title: Now, and only now, the model
scenes.l1: The receipt is sealed. Only now does the AI appear — and all it can do is read the receipt aloud in plain language.
scenes.l2: It cannot add a number, change a status, or "help".
scenes.l3: The provenance line names exactly what produced these words: which model, which build, which path.

scenes.title: Declare every law that exists
scenes.l1: Same request — but now every rule is declared.
scenes.l2: Watch the refusals turn into numbers. One output stays refused forever: no law for it exists anywhere, so no honest system can ever produce it.
scenes.l3: That is the difference between a missing declaration, which the caller can fix, and out of scope, which nobody can.

scenes.title: Try to make the AI lie about that receipt
scenes.l1: {attacks} recorded attempts to talk, trick, or force the AI into changing the receipt — forged receipts, fake authority, smuggled instructions.
scenes.l2: Each one hits a wall before it can touch the answer.
scenes.l3: Three walls, three columns: structure — no path exists; schema — refused at the door; post-validator — the only wall a model's words ever reach.

scenes.title: Proof the guard is alive
scenes.l1: A test that never fails proves nothing.
scenes.l2: So we break the guard on purpose and run the same attacks again: the ones that were blocked now get through, and a withheld output reaches the consumer.
scenes.l3: That is the negative control — the walls are load-bearing, not decorative.

scenes.title: All together
scenes.l1: Everything you just saw, on one screen, live: declare, compute, explain, attack.
